newsitem.title: CANADA: De Beers in deal on Canada diamond project.
newsitem.headline: De Beers in deal on Canada diamond project.

text.p: Partners in a promising diamond property in Canada's Northwest Territories announced Friday an option deal with South Africa's De Beers and plans to consolidate their interests in the project in the hands of Mountain Province Mining Inc.
Mountain Province already holds half of the AK/CJ property while partner Glenmore Highlands Inc owns 40 percent and Camphor Ventures Inc 10 percent.
Under a joint venture deal with De Beers, its Monopros Ltd exploration unit will have the right to earn up to 60 percent of the AK/CJ property, the three Canadian partners said.

"The terms of the joint venture agreement essentially provide that Monopros will earn a 60 percent interest in exchange for conducting an exploration program on the property and a bulk sampling program on one or more new kimberlites, completing a feasibility study on one or more kimberlites, and funding the development and construction of a commercial mine," they said.
De Beers has told the group that based on its initial due diligence it believes there are between four and eight new kimberlitic bodies in the central and eastern part of the claim block.
So far the group has discovered one kimberlite pipe -- AK-5034 -- that contains an estimated 19 million tonnes of ore grading two carats a tonne.
"Obviously De Beers wouldn't be doing this deal if they didn't think there were more (kimberlite pipes)," said Mountain Province president Jan Vandersande. "They really like the property."

De Beers obtained an indepedent valuation for diamonds sampled from the pipe as part of its due diligence but the data have not been released publicly. Vandersande said the value of the stones was "not bad but not fantastic."

Monopros is assuming operatorship of the property and has agreed to immediately buy C$1 million of Mountain Province treasury stock in the form of 209,644 units at a price of C$4.77 each. Each unit will consist of a share and a share purchase warrant to buy a further share at C$6.36.

Mountain Provice and Glenmore also agreed to consolidate their stakes in the property in a deal in which Mountain Province will pay 17 million of its shares. Glenmore, which is 36 percent owned by Lytton Minerals Ltd, will also get to appoint one-quarter of Mountain's board for two years.
Mountain Province will propose a similar offer to Camphor Ventures on comparable terms. Vandersande this would amount to payment of about 4.5 million shares if they struck a deal.
Mountain Province currently has about 24 million shares outstanding.
De Beers has so far been unsuccessful in its efforts to make a major find in Canada's far north where a land-staking rush took hold after a major diamond discovery earlier this decade.

Analysts said the deal with De Beers -- the premier power in the world diamond industry -- was a boost to the AK project but noted that De Beers had struck similar joint venture deals in Canada in the past that so far have not yielded a breakthrough.
Shares in the three Canadian companies were halted pending the announcement. Mountain Province closed Thursday in Vancouver at 5.30. Camphor closed at at 2.50 and Glenmore at 7.75.
